newsitem.title: USA: U.S. farm trade to E.Europe promising -- USDA aide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. farm trade to E.Europe promising -- USDA aide.

text.p: Eastern Europe should remain a growing market for U.S. bulk commodity and high-value farm products even as it becomes more integrated with the European Union, a U.S. Agriculture Department aide said Friday.
"The trick is to find products where we have an advantage," Allan Mustard, agricultural counselor at the U.S. Embassy in Vienna, told Reuters.
For some consumer-ready products, simply coming from the United States may be enough. "American is sexy," Mustard said. "You slap the American flag on anything and you can sell it."
That allure is true even in Austria, which had the good fortune to end up on the Western side of the "iron curtain" after World War II.
Austrians make some of the finest pastries in the world. Yet when Austrian pastry shops offer "American-style donuts" they are thronged with customers, he said.
During "Super Bowl Night" at a hotel in Vienna, "we sold 5,000 bottles of Coors," Mustard said. "This in a country that produces some of the best beer in the world."
Mustard and other overseas U.S. agriculture department members were in town this week for an annual conference.
Back in Vienna, Mustard oversees the department's activities in seven countries -- Austria, Bosnia, Croatia, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovakia and Slovenia.
U.S. agricultural exports to the region roughly total about $500 million annually, Mustard said. But the seven countries are anything but alike.
Austria is a "very wealthy, sophisticated market," while Bosnia has "just come out a war," Mustard said.
